host.title: MPN ownership
host.observation: Current scope assigns control plane/node OS to MPN; no host assessment or live configuration was supplied.

uds.title: UDS architecture
uds.observation: Current scope names Pepr, Istio, Falco, Velero and centralized logging; architecture supplies a mechanism, not observed enforcement.

realm.title: Bundled realm
realm.observation: Realm defaults: failureFactor=5, permanentLockout=false, idle=900s, max=28800s, password policy includes hashing only, events/admin events enabled with 90-day local event retention.

mesh.title: Mesh and policy
mesh.observation: Package chart declares ambient mesh and generated network policy. Disabled chart-local NetworkPolicy and plaintext application URLs do not establish missing mesh enforcement.

logging.title: API logging
logging.observation: Current HTTP logger includes service, request/trace IDs, event, remote address and response status, with secret redaction. Its common bindings do not add authenticated actor identity; other records/correlation must be checked.

logout.title: Browser logout
logout.observation: Current auth store wipes local auth state then invokes OIDC signout. Local storage use alone is not proof that logout fails; replay/expiry/server-side invalidation need tests.

authz.title: Application access control
authz.observation: API guard validates identity and sets tenant/user context; permission guard invokes a permission enforcer when route metadata is present. This is source support, not complete route/tenant coverage.

images.title: Image release process
images.observation: Builder verifies source digests and produces archive hashes; sample values with empty digests do not establish that a built release is unpinned. Assessed release/SBOM/scans still needed.

core-policy.title: core-policy
core-policy.observation: Pepr mutates/validates non-root execution, no privilege escalation and dropped capabilities, including init and ephemeral containers; exemptions are explicit.

core-network.title: core-network
core-network.observation: Operator generates namespace ingress/egress default-deny NetworkPolicy; connectivity requires declared allow rules.

core-mtls.title: core-mtls
core-mtls.observation: Root-namespace PeerAuthentication requires STRICT mTLS. Horizon opts into ambient mesh; in-mesh plaintext-looking URLs are protected by mesh rather than application TLS.

core-gateway.title: core-gateway
core-gateway.observation: Gateway redirects HTTP to HTTPS and requires TLS 1.3 by default, optionally TLS 1.2; credentialName references Kubernetes TLS secrets.

core-accesslog.title: core-accesslog
core-accesslog.observation: Istio access logs go to stdout; path normalization merges slashes, proxies are held until ready, and forwarded certificate details are sanitized.

core-vector.title: core-vector
core-vector.observation: Vector Agent collects Kubernetes pod and node log files, labels namespace/container/host, uses acknowledged disk buffers, and ships continuously to Loki; metrics are exported.

core-loki.title: core-loki
core-loki.observation: Loki uses ambient mesh; ingress is limited to Grafana, Vector, FalcoSidekick and monitoring service identities; object-store egress is declared separately.

core-grafana.title: core-grafana
core-grafana.observation: Grafana disables local login, uses UDS OAuth, maps Admin group to Admin and Auditor to Viewer, and rejects unmatched groups. OAuth secrets are file-mounted.

core-velero.title: core-velero
core-velero.observation: Velero schedules daily backups at 03:00 with 240-hour TTL, but snapshotVolumes=false and snapshotsEnabled=false; default resource backups do not establish PostgreSQL PVC data recovery.

core-falco.title: core-falco
core-falco.observation: Falco loads shipped rule sets, detects runtime behavior and ships Sidekick events to Loki. Alertmanager delivery is commented out; detection is not automatic access revocation.

core-keycloak.title: core-keycloak
core-keycloak.observation: Core uses identity-config 0.32.0, supports X509 and OTP by default; inactivity auto-disable is opt-in, and concurrent-session limit defaults to unlimited (0). This is platform SSO, not Horizon bundled Keycloak.

core-id-realm.title: core-id-realm
core-id-realm.observation: UDS realm defines three-failure lockout, permanentLockout=true, 600-second idle, PBKDF2-SHA256 password policy with 15 characters and classes/history/expiry; JSON event listener is enabled. Some controls remain optional.

core-id-audit.title: core-id-audit
core-id-audit.observation: UDS event listener prints user/admin events to stdout with event fields and UTC timestamps. Vector can collect these without a separately configured app forwarding agent.

app-namespace.title: app-namespace
app-namespace.observation: All declared workload charts target horizon-uds; package supplies dedicated namespace, distinct workload charts and generated deployment credentials.

app-pods.title: app-pods
app-pods.observation: Candidate service chart applies non-root/read-only/no-escalation contexts, Secret references, probes and resource settings. Rendered app pods corroborate those settings; some init containers lack explicit resources.

app-web.title: app-web
app-web.observation: nginx serves a static SPA at /usr/share/nginx/html on port 3000, with try_files fallback, stdout/stderr logs and no configured proxy_pass, CGI or WebDAV locations.

app-web-image.title: app-web-image
app-web-image.observation: Multistage image copies only built Vue assets into the nginx runtime; source maps are removed. No application/OS user-management endpoint is implemented by the static nginx layer.

app-validation.title: app-validation
app-validation.observation: Global interceptor validates declared params/query/headers/JSON with Zod, enforces Content-Type, and fails routes missing a documented exemption/schema; binary/multipart paths are handled separately.

app-error.title: app-error
app-error.observation: Unknown/DB errors map to generic 500 problem details; HTTP transport and internal NATS dispatcher use the same mapper. Explicit application exceptions retain their supplied detail.

app-enforcer.title: app-enforcer
app-enforcer.observation: Permission enforcement resolves user/target and fails closed on missing authorization or unexpected resolution errors. Individual route metadata remains part of coverage.

app-db-role.title: app-db-role
app-db-role.observation: horizon_app is a distinct LOGIN role granted application DML and schema usage, not superuser/DDL by this migration; migrations/admin credentials are separate.

app-db-values.title: app-db-values
app-db-values.observation: DB runs under UID70 with non-root/read-only/no-escalation and dedicated PGDATA PVC; default replica count is one. Only pgaudit preload is configured, not event classes.

app-db-identity.title: app-db-identity
app-db-identity.observation: Separate admin, horizon_app and openfga_app credentials exist. Bundled Keycloak is configured to connect using the admin DB role, a least-privilege candidate gap.

app-db-extensions.title: app-db-extensions
app-db-extensions.observation: Migration installs pgvector/PostGIS and attempts pgaudit, catching pgaudit failures as warnings; installation and effective audit classes must not be assumed from preload.

app-auth-service.title: app-auth-service
app-auth-service.observation: Browser uses OIDC authorization-code flow, PKCE, automatic silent renew and localStorage user state. Local storage is not evidence of missing explicit logout, but idle semantics depend on the IdP.

app-logged-out.title: app-logged-out
app-logged-out.observation: Dedicated logged-out view displays an explicit logout message and return-to-login action.

app-model-profile.title: app-model-profile
app-model-profile.observation: Candidate default permits intra-namespace traffic and broad external HTTPS for chat/ingestion. MPN local inference needs a narrowed, selected model profile; model runtime is not selected here.

pg-logging.title: pg-logging
pg-logging.observation: PostgreSQL18 defaults connection logging disabled and disconnection logging off; failed authentication is always logged. stderr is the default server-log destination.

pgaudit-default.title: pgaudit-default
pgaudit-default.observation: pgAudit18 session audit classes default to none. Preload/CREATE EXTENSION alone does not enable READ/WRITE/ROLE/DDL auditing; log prefix supplies contextual identity fields.

pg-roles.title: pg-roles
pg-roles.observation: PostgreSQL role attributes govern LOGIN, privilege grants and connection limits; default per-role connection limit is unlimited. Superuser bypasses permission checks.

pg-password.title: pg-password
pg-password.observation: PostgreSQL18 defaults password_encryption to SCRAM-SHA-256. Existing persistent data/configuration can override defaults; generated new credentials and selected image must be distinguished from existing volumes.

core-flavors.title: core-flavors
core-flavors.observation: Core distinguishes unicorn (curated FIPS-validated images), registry1 (Iron Bank hardening) and upstream (development/community images). The production hardened offering exists; actual selected flavor/digests and module mapping remain explicit deployment inputs.

app-jwt.title: app-jwt
app-jwt.observation: API uses jose jwtVerify with fixed issuer/audience/JWKS and expiry validation. It performs no online token introspection or logout/session revocation lookup; expected JWT failures are logged at debug level.

app-permission-table.title: app-permission-table
app-permission-table.observation: Append-only role-grant/revocation table includes actor user, subject user, tenant, role, action and timestamp; it does not record every request or failed authorization.

core-hardened-mesh.title: core-hardened-mesh
core-hardened-mesh.observation: Unicorn flavor selects curated istio-pilot-fips and istio-proxy-fips images; ambient ztunnel has its own FIPS image override. This proves the offered implementation, not the flavor of a deployed MPN cluster.

core-strict-keycloak.title: core-strict-keycloak
core-strict-keycloak.observation: Core Keycloak starts with --features=fips and --fips-mode=strict; cgr image handling adds the FIPS JCE security setup. Bundled Horizon Keycloak is a different chart and must not inherit these flags by name alone.

core-provision.title: core-provision
core-provision.observation: Production requires externally supplied gateway TLS chains, Loki/Velero object stores and a Keycloak database/user. Core cannot determine the supplied CA approvals, storage encryption or bucket lifecycle by itself.

app-ci.title: app-ci
app-ci.observation: Build workflow defines image scanning, unit/integration/E2E gates, coverage report artifacts and digest-bound releases. Configured jobs do not prove execution for an unspecified delivered release.

app-codeql.title: app-codeql
app-codeql.observation: CodeQL runs for code changes and on a weekly schedule with SARIF artifacts and reviewed suppression processing.

app-updates.title: app-updates
app-updates.observation: Weekly automation resolves security advisories and opens labelled security-update PRs; a PR is not proof of delivered patch currency.

app-review-process.title: app-review-process
app-review-process.observation: Scanner findings/suppressions require justification, reviewer approval and linked tracking with expiry/review criteria.

re-images-vendor.title: re-images-vendor
re-images-vendor.observation: Vendor documents FIPS images configured in approved-only mode; using these images is concrete enabled configuration, not an unconfigured capability. FIPS apps do not require host kernel FIPS because validated user-space entropy is included.

re-images-node-mode.title: re-images-node-mode
re-images-node-mode.observation: Vendor explicitly says node-fips Crypto APIs are configured into approved mode at image build time through openssl-config-fipshardened, without application code changes.

re-images-nist5132.title: re-images-nist5132
re-images-nist5132.observation: NIST lists Chainguard FIPS Provider for OpenSSL, FIPS140-3 certificate5132, Active, sunset2031-01-13, approved-mode caveat. Exact API/web/Postgres SBOM markers map to this certificate; no certificate number guessed from generic FIPS naming.

re-images-verify.title: re-images-verify
re-images-verify.observation: Real signer verification uses pinned DU Fulcio/Sigstore TSA anchors, expected subject/SAN/issuer, P256/SHA256 DSSE signature, code-signing EKU and RFC3161 timestamp. release.py check_evidence calls verify_production for all required phases and binds exact archives/build-info/packed image digests; CAT vouch gates publication. Actual delivery run succeeded these gates.

re-images-publish.title: re-images-publish
re-images-publish.observation: The main-only protected release workflow selects qualified successful main source, validates image inventory/source digests against packed OCI manifests, binds archive SHA256SUMS, requires cryptographically verified Witness evidence and CAT vouch before registry publication; digest-qualified registry bundle fixes installation content.

re-images-core-identity.title: re-images-core-identity
re-images-core-identity.observation: Core1.14 always starts Keycloak --features=fips --fips-mode=strict. identity-config0.32 stages bc-fips/bctls/bcutil jars via keycloak-crypto-fips1402 and syncs these providers; supported hardened flavors exist. Actual contract selects this shared identity, so web/API session and authentication crypto belongs here, not missing bundled Keycloak settings. Actual Horizon contract does not select the Core distribution flavor.

re-images-identity-libs.title: re-images-identity-libs
re-images-identity-libs.observation: Identity-config stages required BouncyCastle FIPS provider jars from its version-matched Keycloak FIPS dependency; sync.sh copies these into Keycloak provider directory when FIPS_ENABLED.

re-images-keycloak-fips.title: re-images-keycloak-fips
re-images-keycloak-fips.observation: Upstream documents that --features=fips --fips-mode=strict uses BouncyCastle FIPS approved mode; session generation/authentication crypto can be delegated to the actual UDS identity service.

re-images-scans.title: re-images-scans
re-images-scans.observation: Actual qualified run42109769948 succeeded per-image Grype/SBOM and ClamAV jobs, with retained API/web reports; reused PostgreSQL has its own verified prior build/scan evidence. Weekly dependency security-update automation exists. Release packaging scans have a narrower scope than source and application-image scans.

re-images-maintained.title: re-images-maintained
re-images-maintained.observation: Vendor states FIPS product variants are maintained with daily rebuilds and CVE SLA. Selected delivery is Nov5 (five days before this review) with explicit supported product versions and recent scan records, rather than an unknown model-server implementation substituted for delivered products.

re-images-signer.title: re-images-signer
re-images-signer.observation: Production signs exact artifacts with downloaded Witness0.12.0; wrapper creates local capture using OpenSSL and invokes Witness keyless signer. Its closed environment excludes GODEBUG. Upstream exact Linux binary inspected with go version -m: go1.26.5, CGO_ENABLED=0, no GOFIPS140 build setting. Application FIPS image SBOMs do not cover this separate CI signing/hash process.

re-images-witness-binary.title: re-images-witness-binary
re-images-witness-binary.observation: Pinned UDM setup source downloads upstream Witness0.12.0 Linux amd64 and verifies its Sigstore release signature. That exact binary was downloaded read-only and inspected (not executed) with go version -m; no GOFIPS140/GODEBUG FIPS build setting is recorded. It uses native Go crypto rather than the application OpenSSL provider.

re-images-go-fips.title: re-images-go-fips
re-images-go-fips.observation: Go documentation says GOFIPS140 default is off and fips140 GODEBUG defaults off unless enabled at build time; approved algorithms alone are not proof of validated approved-mode operation. This is separate from successful DSSE signature verification.

re-images-logging.title: re-images-logging
re-images-logging.observation: Core centralizes logs and supplies TLS/network/access controls. No log record/batch cryptographic hash-and-sign configuration was found in the shipped Loki/Vector settings; transport integrity alone does not implement the exact retained-log signing alternative asked by V204739.

re-images-registry-check.title: re-images-registry-check
re-images-registry-check.observation: Read-only ECR metadata Nov10: registry scanType BASIC, rules[]; horizon-api/web/postgres repository scanOnPush=false. CI supplies actual per-build scanning, but no configured continuous rescan of the fixed delivered inventory was found in these settings. This source ECR evidence is not a statement about a separate DU/MPN scanner.

re-images-nats-purejs.observation: Actual delivered API image0e20f5f... was exported read-only. Runtime package@nats-io/nkeys2.0.3 lib/nacl.js imports tweetnacl1.0.3; kp.js sign() calls nacl.sign.detached. File hashes: nkeys kp.js95678dc5fee2f88470cdb1dd8131f9275a359198e794b31563bc2bcb2ea267e2; nacl.js85bbc7f2b9c47265dc3e50c390f8a84104e7f2f37ef772ffd03af9a659492834; tweetnacl-fast6bcd37a3b20dce913f82d4b23e4e2b661058b4b953df8a3f8c45d56ac4f72447. Source uses these keys to sign NATS user/account authenticationJWTs and nonce authenticators. FIPS OpenSSL image does not validate this pureJS implementation.

re-images-jose-webcrypto.title: re-images-jose-webcrypto
re-images-jose-webcrypto.observation: Actual delivered jose6.2.13 implementation dist/webapi/lib/jws_verify.js calls crypto.subtle.verify; OIDC JWT verification therefore uses NodeWebCrypto in the validated FIPS image. The separate NATS JWT signature path uses @nats-io/nkeys/tweetnacl and must not be conflated with this OIDC implementation.

re-governance-scm.title: re-governance-scm
re-governance-scm.observation: Version-controlled release/SCM process identifies ticket-to-PR-to-SHA-to-release/digest traceability, roles, approval gates, release tracks, immutable artifacts and impact classification. Document is a draft RFC; implemented workflows and live rules corroborate specific mechanisms rather than assuming every planned phase is delivered.

re-governance-change.title: re-governance-change
re-governance-change.observation: Executable workflow classifies changed security-sensitive paths plus mandatory author ATO-impact declaration; resolves higher impact, requires significant control-family rationale, labels changes and rejects declaration mismatch.

re-governance-rules.title: re-governance-rules
re-governance-rules.observation: Read live active main ruleset Nov10:1approving review, CODEOWNERS review, stale-approval dismissal, integration/unit/E2E tests, CodeQL both languages, impact classifier and change metadata checks. Admin role has configured bypass; legacy branch-protection404 was not lack of protection.

re-governance-review-example.title: re-governance-review-example
re-governance-review-example.observation: Merged Nov10 after independent member approval and recorded ATO-impact/class labels; concrete code-review and change-control evidence, not merely an unexecuted policy.

re-governance-review.title: re-governance-review
re-governance-review.observation: Security findings/suppressions require source-controlled justification, named reviewer approval, linked defect tickets and accepted expiry/classification. Security sensitive paths are CODEOWNERS routed.

re-governance-owners.title: re-governance-owners
re-governance-owners.observation: Security/compliance/supply-chain paths route to horizon-security; database changes route to horizon-infra. This is concrete security-review responsibility assignment, not proof of annual training.

re-governance-release-build.title: re-governance-release-build
re-governance-release-build.observation: Actual delivered appb84 build19710 completed successfully Nov5. Read/downloaded11Grype SARIF artifacts and APIintegration coverage. Integration and E2E gates succeeded. Grype artifacts contain tracked high-severity findings; successful build is not a claim of zero vulnerabilities.

re-governance-release-codeql.title: re-governance-release-codeql
re-governance-release-codeql.observation: Successful CodeQL at actual delivered b84SHA. Downloaded rawSARIF:JavaScript/TypeScript0results,Python11sensitive-logging results; matching source allowlist explicitly classifies correlationUUID false positives with reviewer/ticket references.

re-governance-allowlist.title: re-governance-allowlist
re-governance-allowlist.observation: Eleven Python logging findings are individually hash-bound false-positive dispositions with rationale, approved_by and linked GALtickets; not blanket UI dismissal.

re-governance-source-coverage.title: re-governance-source-coverage
re-governance-source-coverage.observation: API tests enable v8source coverage with text/lcov reports, four80percent thresholds and specified report directory. Other packages have analogous coverage settings. Actual APIintegration artifact separately retains operation/status coverage; those are different metrics.

re-governance-updates.title: re-governance-updates
re-governance-updates.observation: Scheduled weekly advisory updates create labelled securityPRs and tracking through maintained release branches, corroborated by scan/release pipeline; formal exception/SLA decisions remain reviewable inputs.

re-governance-flows.title: re-governance-flows
re-governance-flows.observation: Sequence/data-flow design documents15second request deadlines,3attempt retry/backoff, circuit breaker after5failed calls, independent transactions and bounded concurrency. Specific mitigations address unbounded waits and service recursion risk.

re-governance-db-timeout.title: re-governance-db-timeout
re-governance-db-timeout.observation: Application database pool startup sets statement_timeout12000ms under the documented15second transport timeout; implementation corroborates the bounded-wait design.

re-governance-architecture.title: re-governance-architecture
re-governance-architecture.observation: Architecture/data model documentation describes application elements, service boundaries and storage; does not itself supply a contract-specific CUI taxonomy or a complete approved MPN disaster-recovery plan.

re-governance-policy-ia.title: re-governance-policy-ia
re-governance-policy-ia.observation: Corporate draft identity policy prohibits shared interactive CUI accounts, mandates unique users and identity-verified administrator recovery; header Draft / Effective TBD means no approval or completed recovery event is asserted.

re-governance-policy-ac.title: re-governance-policy-ac
re-governance-policy-ac.observation: Corporate draft access policy defines quarterly access certification and retained review evidence; it does not provide a dated GitHub repository certification result.

re-governance-policy-ir.title: re-governance-policy-ir
re-governance-policy-ir.observation: Written corporate incident/violation reporting procedure defines severity, reporting, containment, preservation, responsibilities and review; draft header and follow-on runbook/contact-sheetTBD retained as limitations.

re-governance-policy-cp.title: re-governance-policy-cp
re-governance-policy-cp.observation: Corporate draft explicitly leaves per-system RTO/RPO, backup configuration/test schedule and actual BCP/DRP TBD. A general commitment is not an application recovery plan or protected-assets procedure.

re-governance-policy-au.title: re-governance-policy-au
re-governance-policy-au.observation: Draft corporate audit policy specifies quarterly review, retained reports and responsible security roles; no completed MPN audit-review report/date found.

re-governance-policy-classification.title: re-governance-policy-classification
re-governance-policy-classification.observation: Written corporate classification policy defines broad sensitivity tiers and handling/marking obligations; approved systems list isTODO and contract-specific CUI categories remain an open SSP decision.

re-governance-policy-training.title: re-governance-policy-training
re-governance-policy-training.observation: Corporate policy identifies recurring security/awareness courses in ThreatSwitch and annual/role-based training requirements. It does not establish annual SDLC security-course completion by every application manager/designer/developer/tester.

re-governance-policy-backlog.title: re-governance-policy-backlog
re-governance-policy-backlog.observation: Company controlled policy backlog explicitly distinguishes written procedures from operational adoption; CUIcategories/boundary and some access/training evidence remain open. Only concise control observations are reproduced here; no personnel roster.

re-governance-policy-asset.title: re-governance-policy-asset

re-asd-id-events.title: re-asd-id-events
